::: {#sol-shift-lse}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{LSE}(\vz)
&= \log \sumto{k}{C} \e{z_k}
&& \text{(definition of $\operatorname{LSE}$)} \\
&= \log \sumto{k}{C} \e{c} \e{z_k - c}
&& \text{(add and subtract $c$ in each exponent)} \\
&= \log \paren{\e{c} \sumto{k}{C} \e{z_k - c}}
&& \text{(take $\e{c}$ out of the sum)} \\
&= c + \log \sumto{k}{C} \e{z_k - c}
&& \text{(log of a product)} \\
&= c + \operatorname{LSE}(\vz - c)
&& \text{(definition of $\operatorname{LSE}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Take $c = \max_k z_k$.
Then every exponent $z_k - c$ is at most 0, so no exponential exceeds 1,
and one exponent is exactly 0, so the sum is at least 1 and its log is not $-\infty$.

:::
